## Purpose and Entrypoints
Scion is a Go-based orchestration platform for isolated, concurrent “deep agents” running in containers or remote runtimes. The primary CLI binary is `cmd/scion/main.go`, whose command tree in `cmd/root.go` manages projects, agents, messaging, templates, and server modes. `cmd/sciontool/main.go` is the in-agent companion binary for harness lifecycle, credentials, hooks, metadata, services, and telemetry. `cmd/server.go` starts the local Workstation or Hub control-plane modes.

## Agent Provisioning and Execution
The agent layer resolves a requested template, configuration, credentials, workspace, and runtime into a runnable agent container. `pkg/agent/manager.go` and `pkg/agent/provision.go` own lifecycle/provisioning; `pkg/agent/run.go` launches the resolved agent. Runtime abstraction separates orchestration from execution backends: `pkg/runtime/interface.go`, `pkg/runtime/factory.go`, and implementations for Docker, Podman, Apple Container, Cloud Run, and Kubernetes under `pkg/runtime/`. Workspace backends support local directories, worktrees, NFS, Cloud Run volumes, and GKE shared volumes.

## Templates, Harnesses, and In-Container Control
Templates define agent prompts, home setup, skills, and harness selection; embedded defaults live in `resources/templates/default/` and repository templates in `.scion/templates/`. `pkg/harness/harness.go` and `pkg/harness/resolve.go` normalize harness-specific behavior, authentication, and bundle installation. Harness images/configurations are maintained under `harnesses/`, e.g. `harnesses/claude/config.yaml` and `harnesses/gemini-cli/scion_harness.py`. Inside a launched container, `pkg/sciontool/supervisor/supervisor.go` manages the harness process, while `pkg/sciontool/hooks/` adapts harness events into Scion lifecycle/status/telemetry behavior.

## Hub Control Plane and Authorization
The optional Hub is an HTTP control plane assembled in `pkg/hub/server.go`, with route registration and API handlers centered in `pkg/hub/handlers.go`. It governs agents, projects, templates, secrets, runtime brokers, schedules, workspace access, and web clients. Authentication and authorization are first-class boundaries: `pkg/hub/auth.go`, `pkg/hub/authorize.go`, and `pkg/hub/authz_kernel.go` evaluate identity, operation, role/policy bindings, scopes, delegation, and access constraints before handlers act. Hub clients used by the CLI and brokers are in `pkg/hubclient/client.go` and related endpoint modules.

## Persistent State, Secrets, and Object Storage
Domain persistence is modeled with Ent schemas in `pkg/ent/schema/` and implemented through storage-facing interfaces/adapters in `pkg/store/store.go` and `pkg/store/entadapter/`. The model includes users, projects, agents, conversations, roles/policies, credentials, broker dispatch, schedules, skills, and templates. SQLite and PostgreSQL are supported through `pkg/ent/entc/driver_sqlite.go` and `pkg/ent/entc/driver_postgres.go`; PostgreSQL is the material HA datastore. Secrets are isolated behind `pkg/secret/backend.go`, with local encrypted and GCP Secret Manager implementations. Files/resources can use local storage or GCS via `pkg/storage/storage.go` and `pkg/storage/gcs.go`.

## Messaging, Brokers, and Distributed Dispatch
Agent/user messages are normalized, validated, persisted, and rendered through `pkg/messaging/envelope.go`, `pkg/messaging/delivery.go`, and `pkg/messaging/resolve.go`. The Hub routes control and messaging requests to runtime brokers; broker routing/authentication lives in `pkg/hub/broker_routing.go` and `pkg/hub/brokerauth.go`. A broker exposes execution against its local runtimes through `pkg/runtimebroker/server.go` and `pkg/runtimebroker/handlers.go`, maintaining Hub connectivity and heartbeats. External chat systems are plugin boundaries using the gRPC broker protocol in `proto/broker/v1/broker.proto` and plugin manager in `pkg/plugin/manager.go`; implementations reside in `extras/scion-telegram/`, `extras/scion-discord/`, `extras/scion-slack/`, and `extras/scion-teams/`.

## Interfaces, Observability, and Deployment
The browser UI is a Vite/TypeScript client embedded into the Go server (`web/embed.go`), with application startup in `web/src/client/main.ts` and API/SSE access in `web/src/client/api.ts` and `web/src/client/sse-client.ts`. Telemetry is collected in agent containers by `pkg/sciontool/telemetry/pipeline.go`; Hub metrics/tracing are exposed through `pkg/hub/metrics.go` and `pkg/observability/`. GCP integrations include Cloud Run, GKE, GCS, IAM, Secret Manager, Cloud Logging, and OpenTelemetry/GCP metrics. Hub deployment is packaged as a Kubernetes Helm chart in `deploy/helm/scion-hub/`, while `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.hub` provide main image entrypoints.
